title: ProtocolLab Package Producer Boundary Work Item
summary: Harden the quic-dotnet ProtocolLab package producer so HTTP/3 and raw QUIC packages stay lane-separated and raw QUIC never falls back to managed HTTP/3 helpers.
planned_changes:
- Keep package v2 templates aligned with `providedImplementations` metadata and package-local manifests.
- Keep `quic-dotnet-dev` HTTP/3-only and `quic-dotnet-raw-dev` raw-QUIC-only.
- Guard raw package generation so adapter/server project paths resolve under the quic-dotnet repository root.
- Guard raw run submission so H3 protocol/scenario/capability selections fail before packaging, upload, or controller submission.
- Update operator docs for the enforced package boundary.
- Run focused template tests and package dry-runs for the H3 and raw package targets when locally supported.
out_of_scope: Broadening raw QUIC scenarios beyond `quic.transport.multiplex.100x64kb` and `quic.transport.duplex-streams`.
Routing raw QUIC validation through managed HTTP/3 helpers.
Depending on public ProtocolLab concrete production adapter projects for quic-dotnet implementation source.
Claiming rack-lab performance provenance without a controller job, package SHA-256, run ID, and outcome artifact.
verification_plan: Run `ProtocolLabPackageTemplateTests`, run H3 and raw package generation dry-runs when the sibling ProtocolLab package builder is locally available, inspect produced package IDs, versions, manifests, and SHA-256 values, validate touched SpecTrace JSON, and run diff hygiene checks.
